passages.v03:c37:p0029: The packed days passed quickly, and tests reached their conclusion. Nell earned High Honors in English. Honora earned Honors in Classics, whereas Cressy did so in Mathematics. Mabel achieved a respectable overall performance. Subsequently, Convocation took place.
passages.v03:c37:p0031: Nell pondered the reason Hugh had gifted her flowers for Convocation. Throughout the previous winter, she had encountered him on very few occasions. Since the Christmas holidays, his visits to Tabby’s Place amounted to just a single Friday evening, and their encounters in other locations were infrequent. It was clear to her that his intense focus on his studies was aimed at achieving High Honors and the Cooper Prize, leaving him minimal involvement in Wexcombe's social activities. In contrast, Nell’s own winter had contained a great deal of social entertainment. Her interactions with the Gardners had been frequent; her bond with Dorothy was extremely close; and within college circles, the news of her engagement to Cyril was anticipated at any moment. Nell was anticipating it as well. Nevertheless, right before departing Tabby’s Place to attend Convocation, she discarded Cyril’s violets and substituted Hugh’s lilies-of-the-valley. The motive behind her action was something she was unable to explain. For some reason, as her long-held ambitions were being realized, past Brierley times, aspirations, and companionships felt remarkably near. In former times, she and Hugh had playfully imagined the occasion when they would both be graduates in Arts, wearing caps and gowns. That extraordinary day had finally arrived, and Cyril’s violets did not fit into it. Only the blossoms from her long-standing friend appeared to suit this realization of early-blooming dreams that he had formerly shared.
